title: What If We Burned Every Fossil Fuel on Earth?

scenes.text: What if we burned all the coal, oil and gas? Antarctica would almost lose its ice.
Scientists modeled about 10,000 billion tonnes of carbon, roughly the total of all recoverable fuel.
That releases within about 500 years, and the planet would warm by more than 10 degrees Celsius.
Antarctica holds ice for 58 meters of sea level. At this much carbon, it nearly all goes.
Melting is slow: about 3 meters of sea level per century during the first thousand years.
Even ten thousand years later, Earth would still be several degrees warmer. In the researchers' words: burn it all, melt it all.

description:
What if humans burned every fossil fuel that can be dug up?
A 2015 study in Science Advances found it would almost eliminate Antarctica's ice and raise seas by more than 50 meters, over thousands of years.
